To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the structure and function of the dimeric SLC26 transporter is determined by the STAS domain.
SLC26 dimmers are stabilized through the STAS domain, that the SLC26 dimers are functional dimers and that the STAS domain is involved in this functional cooperativity.
we determined the structure of an embedded SLC26 dumer and identified the functional role of the STAS domain in SLC26 dymers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural basis of functional interactions in dimerying SLC26 transport proteins.
the structural characterization of the SLC26 family and the elucidation of the structural basis of functional interactions between protomers in dimers.
the structure and function of membrane proteins
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work presents the first structural and functional insight into SLC26 transport proteins, which are important in human physiology and pathophysiology.
the structural and functional data presented here define the framework for mechanistic understanding of SLC26 dimeric structure and function.
the dimerization of SLC26s is a functional requirement for their activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have determined the structure of a dimeric SLC26 transporter in the membrane, and that the structure is functionally relevant.
we provide the first structural model for a SLC26 dier and show how this dier stabilizes the protein and how the dier interacts with its functional partners.
we were able to determine a structure of an SLO26 dimer in a lipid bilayer and to characterize the functional relevance of the dimer interface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SLC26 dimers have a unique interface compared to the SLC4/23 family.
the STAS domain of SLC26 proteins is essential for the dimerization of SLC26 family proteins.
we have determined the structure of an ion transporter dimer embedded in lipid membrane and that we have identified the structural elements that are important for functional cooperativity.
